descripcion: At B2 feedback names what happened and what to change, kept separate from a judgement of character. The full four-slot structure with an acknowledged limit (C1) isn't the target yet — describing behaviour and suggesting a change clearly is enough.

filas: The report had a few mistakes in it.
Maybe double-check the numbers next time.

ejemplos.texto: The report had a few mistakes in the numbers.
Maybe it would help to double-check before sending it.
Can I give you some quick feedback on that?

notas: Asking permission first (can I give you some feedback?) makes the rest much easier to accept.
Describing behaviour instead of character avoids sounding like a personal attack.
One suggestion at a time is more useful than a long list of everything that could be improved.

contraste.es: Spanish can separate the action from the person (el informe tenía errores – the report had some errors, rather than eres descuidado – you're careless). English feedback relies on exactly this separation, so the action-focused form is worth using consistently.
contraste.de: German uses the same separation (der Bericht hatte einige Fehler rather than du bist schlampig), and ehrlich gesagt corresponds to to be honest. Constructive feedback therefore transfers directly.
contraste.it: Italian uses the same separation (nel rapporto c'erano degli errori rather than sei distratto), so constructive feedback transfers directly.
contraste.fr: French uses the same separation (le rapport contenait quelques erreurs rather than tu es négligent), so constructive feedback transfers directly.
contraste.pt: Portuguese uses the same separation (o relatório tinha alguns erros rather than és descuidado), so constructive feedback transfers directly.

errores: Judging character instead of describing behaviour: you're disorganised instead of the files weren't labelled clearly.
Giving feedback without asking permission first.
Giving several pieces of feedback at once instead of focusing on one.

autochequeo: Is the feedback about behaviour, not character?
Was permission asked before giving feedback?
Is only one main point given, not a long list?
Is there a clear, specific suggestion for next time?
Would the other person know exactly what to change?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on how the feedback is given. Check whether it describes behaviour rather than character, and whether it includes a specific, actionable suggestion. Do not rewrite the text.
